title: Shading and Sky-First Composite in Rainbow Mountain (Clone-Paint Workflow Demonstration)

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata from video file; approximate unless transcript confirms exact date

summary: The video presents a Photoshop workflow focused on creating three-dimensional shading through a directional light, merging sky and landscape, and iterative RAW processing. It emphasizes painting light with brushes (including clone-paint), replacing or reorienting sky, and blending multiple passes of RAW edits (including curves, split toning, and color grading) to achieve a cohesive, lit landscape. Key tactics include avoiding heavy selections, using large brushes for broad shading, performing a sky flip for directional lighting, and employing a clone-smear bleed to smooth sky transitions into the foreground. The presenter also demonstrates color and luminosity adjustments on reds and yellows to enhance perceived sunlit contrast, followed by final touch-ups with dodge/burn and sponge tools to sculpt depth.

sections.title: Establishing shading and sky integration
sections.description: Intro covers establishing a directional light to give the main ridge more space on the lighted side and emphasizes fusing the sky with the landscape to avoid a hard edge across the scene.

sections.title: RAW workflow planning and sky separation
sections.description: Discusses flattening a flat image in RAW for a broader palette, then planning to adjust the sky separately via RAW (including the possibility of treating the sky as a smart object) with several approaches to re-enter RAW.

sections.title: Sky/land fusion and early sky grading
sections.description: Explains fusing background layers with the sky, reducing highlights, and introducing a strong curve to begin separating sky from land, including an initial plan to apply a blur to merge the two regions more organically.

sections.title: Directional light painting and edge refinement
sections.description: Key section where the presenter paints light onto the ridges using broad brushes, discusses not relying on selections, and uses clone-paint to adjust color and brightness with careful edge control and incremental light application.

sections.title: Sky orientation and color grading via RAW iterations
sections.description: Describes flipping the sky to orient the light source, then adjusting RAW curves and color to create a gradient that supports the new lighting direction, including a half-saturation approach and splitting tones for sky color.

sections.title: Sky bleed, dodge highlights, and color polish
sections.description: Demonstrates bleeding sky detail into the background with 30% opacity clone-smear, applying highlight dodge to intensify sunlit edges, and performing targeted color tweaks (e.g., reds) to sustain color separation and depth.

sections.title: Final pass, curvature, and closing observations
sections.description: Concludes with fine-tuning of curvature on slopes, selective color sharpening, and reinforcing the directional light concept as the central driver of depth and viewer guidance; ends with a final before/after and brief closing remarks.

featured_techniques.technique: Sky replacement via sky flip and color grading
Sky bleed using clone-smear at 30% opacity
RAW multi-pass workflow with sky isolation (smart object approach)
Curves-based sky grading and split toning
Selective color adjustments and luminance manipulation (reds/yellows)
